open_points.subject: capturing an equal failed execution
open_points.text: “an equal case is that case. The corpus digest changes; the serving implementation keeps serving and visibly lacks a verdict over the current corpus” contradicts A04 rule 1–2, under which an equal case keeps its existing corpus place and therefore leaves the corpus digest unchanged.
open_points.question: When capture resolves to an existing equal TrialCase, does the corpus and its current AdmissionVerdict remain unchanged, or is capture intended to create some new corpus fact despite equal case identity?
options: Keep the existing case, corpus digest and applicable verdict unchanged
Treat the capture as a new corpus addition with a new digest
Keep the case but invalidate existing verdicts by another recorded fact
open_points.default_guess: Keep the existing case, corpus digest and applicable verdict unchanged.

open_points.subject: trial fixture publication before its TrialCase record
open_points.text: The flows first send file bytes through “capability:store.put_value_bytes” and only afterward write the StoredValues and TrialCase through “capability:store.record_change”; yet they also say “a store call that fails changes nothing” and that trial-case fixtures are the only files kept beyond a run.
open_points.question: What happens to content-addressed file bytes already published when the later record_change fails?
options: Publish the bytes and records atomically in one store operation
Delete unreferenced bytes after the failed record write
Retain unreferenced bytes as an explicit exception
open_points.default_guess: Publish the bytes and records atomically so no unreferenced fixture remains.

open_points.subject: effect output files when the kernel stops before recording the outcome
open_points.text: “a file the service returns goes to the run's spool through capability:store.spool_file. A second store call writes the outcome” and “a crash between the in_flight record and the outcome record leaves the attempt in_flight, turned unknown at the next start” do not state what happens to a file spooled after the response but before that second store call.
open_points.question: When recovery turns such an attempt into unknown, who removes or retains its unrecorded spooled output, and does it continue to count toward the run spool ceiling?
options: Remove every unrecorded output of the recovered attempt
Retain it and count it toward the run spool ceiling until the whole spool is removed
Add a SpooledFile record while recovering the unknown attempt
open_points.default_guess: Remove every unrecorded output of the recovered attempt.

open_points.subject: store failure during startup recovery
open_points.text: The general rule says “a store call that fails changes nothing ... and the request is answered as an internal error,” but recover_in_flight_attempts and recover_running_runs make store calls before the surface accepts any request, when there is no request to answer; the startup Errors section states no outcome for such a failure.
open_points.question: What must surface do if a store read, record change or spool removal fails during startup recovery?
options: Abort startup immediately and leave the surface closed
Continue startup with the records already recovered
open_points.default_guess: Abort startup immediately and leave the surface closed.
